subject: Sales discovery: quantization trade-offs & eval plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@avatech.com>, Mike Lee <mike.lee@avatech.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sales discovery recap & next steps — quantization / evals

Hi Sarah + Mike,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion and appreciate the clear context on latency targets (tail p95 < 250ms for single-turn prompts) and the quality bar for customer-facing summarization. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goals we captured: reduce token cost ~3-5x vs current baseline while maintaining >92% quality parity on your summarization eval set.
- Primary workloads: single-turn prompt generation + short chat-like followups (~80 tokens typical).
- Constraints: must run in us-west region; data residency ok with hosted API but need audit log export.

Next steps (proposed):
1) SE-led evaluation: Redwood to run model-fit experiments on your eval prompt set (please see attached prompt set) across candidate models (Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and a tuned 13B variant) with AWQ and GPTQ quantization profiles and FP8 baseline. Deliverable: CSV with throughput/latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.
2) Joint review call next week to go over results & recommended model+quantization profile.
3) If results look good, we’ll scope a 30-day pilot on Dedicated capacity for production validation.

Attachments: avatech_eval_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (prompt set), NDA-Avatech-signed.pdf

I’ve looped in Dev (SE) to lead the evals. Dev — can you confirm timing for the first run and whether you need any additional data from Avatech?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0137

Subject: Re: Sales discovery recap & next steps — quantization / evals

Thanks Marissa — I started the baseline runs this morning. Quick notes on plan and what I’ll deliver:

Plan (first run, 48-72h):
- Models: Llama-2-13b-chat (fp16 baseline), Mistral-7b-Instruct, and a tuned 13B variant we’ve validated for Redwood runtime.
- Quantization/profiles: AWQ-4bit (fastest throughput), GPTQ-4bit (quality-focused), and FP8 (if available on target infra) as a baseline for accuracy.
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency (single and batch sizes), tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens estimate, and accuracy metrics we compute from your labeled summarization set (ROUGE-L, exact match on key fields, and a small human-preference sampling).
- Output: avatech_benchmark_results.csv + short slide with recommended profile per workload.

Early expectations: AWQ usually gives the best throughput for generation-heavy single-turn workflows at modest quality impact for 7B models; GPTQ on 13B often preserves quality better but gives lower throughput. FP8 (on supported kernels) can be a strong baseline for quality but may not hit your latency SLO unless we combine with autoscaling/batching.

Questions for Avatech:
1) Can you confirm the percentage of your requests that are single-turn completions vs multi-turn? (Marissa noted ~85% single-turn)
2) Any non-English user segments we should include?

I’ll share the first CSV once the run completes. If results look promising, we should plan a 30–45 minute call with engineering next week to validate production constraints (KV cache warming, p95 degradation on bursts).

- Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa and Dev — this looks great and aligned with what we discussed. A few quick answers and asks: 

- Confirming: ~82% single-turn, ~18% multi-turn support flows.
- We do have a small Spanish cohort (~6%) — if it’s straightforward to include, please do.
- Timing: our engineering lead (Mike) is available for the joint review on Mon 2 Aug between 10–11am PT.

Also, two asks: 
1) Can you include a short human-preference sample (5–10 examples) comparing AWQ vs GPTQ on the tuned 13B for our key summarization prompts? That will help our product folks judge subtle regressions.
2) Please include estimated cost numbers at both hosted and Dedicated reservation levels — we’re trying to justify Dedicated if the quality tradeoffs are acceptable.

We’ve uploaded our larger audit logs extract to the Drive link in case you need more context (link shared separately).

Best,
